summary: A is substantially closer to the frozen contract and is the safer patch to review, although it still needs revision before merge because Upload bypasses FilesService.Add and its tests omit required validation and source-reader failure coverage.
reasons: A preserves Add and narrowly adds the requested Upload API using internal/multipartbody.NewFile with the required field name, filename, buffered replayable body, options, and response semantics.
A’s retry test uses a wrapped reader and verifies that the multipart filename and content survive a 429 retry.
Both patches violate the explicit requirement to route Upload through FilesService.Add; each duplicates Add’s request, decoding, and missing-data logic instead.

B directly contradicts scope constraints by adding WithFilesFormFields and association-field machinery, despite the contract saying not to add association fields and to add exactly the specified convenience API while keeping FilesOption behavior unchanged list of allowed additions implicit in contract). B also refactors unrelated retry behavior and changes Raw.Do reader-ownership semantics globally type consequence visible in changelog/code). B modifies multipart helper with an extra API and broadens docs/tests significantly, adding review surface unrelated to required buffered Upload path.
risks_a: Upload duplicates Add rather than delegating to it, so future option, request, decoding, or error changes can diverge.
No visible Upload tests cover empty filename, nil content, or propagation of a failing source reader.
Validation combines two distinct invalid inputs into one error and constructs options before validating inputs, which is less precise and could run option callbacks unnecessarily.
risks_b: Adds prohibited association fields and changes FilesOption behavior through WithFilesFormFields.
Makes broad, unrelated changes to Raw.Do retry and body-closing semantics, potentially affecting every seekable request body.

Its GetBody closure reuses and mutates the same seeker rather than creating independent readers, creating fragile transport behavior and possible concurrency hazards type visible shared seeker). It also still bypasses Add in Upload and duplicates its logic. No visible test covers source-reader failure propagation.
